name: Premiere One-Word Pop-Fade Captions
use_when: A Reel, Short, or TikTok-style edit needs fast one-word subtitle energy.
Premiere auto captions are useful as a timing draft but need custom style and motion.
Captions should feel clean, modern, and energetic without becoming a separate visual stack.
A finished AE animation render needs captions only in the sections where visual text does not already carry the line.
avoid_when: The project needs accessibility-first full subtitle lines.
The subject is serious testimony where fast pop captions would cheapen the tone.
The frame already has hook text, proof cards, or B-roll text carrying the idea.

timeline_pattern.pattern: transcribe_sequence -> create_short_captions -> style_one_caption -> apply_style -> correct_timing -> upgrade_to_graphics -> add_transform_pop_fade -> save_preset -> apply_to_selected_text
timeline_pattern.draft_rule: Treat Premiere generated captions as a draft until wording, timing, chunking, and placement are checked.
timeline_pattern.conversion_rule: Upgrade captions to graphics only after the caption content and placement are correct.
timeline_pattern.placement_rule: Use a lower-third position that avoids faces, hands, products, proof, and platform UI.
timeline_pattern.suppression_rule: After upgrading to graphics, disable or fade captions during animation-heavy sections that already communicate the words.
timeline_pattern.impact_rule: If styling individual words, emphasize the impact word rather than the word auto-captioning happens to isolate.

motion.rule: Use a short position-and-opacity pop so the word arrives quickly and settles before it needs to be read.

keyframe_values.caption_chunking: Start with about 7 characters for one-word social style or 10-15 characters for slightly fuller high-quality Reel captions; keep single-line chunks when the frame has animation text.
keyframe_values.text_size: Around 60 in a 1080x1920 Premiere vertical sequence is a usable starting point; adjust for font and safe area.
keyframe_values.position_opacity: End keyframe at final position and 100% opacity; start keyframe slightly lower with 0% opacity.
keyframe_values.easing: Ease so the caption starts fast and slows into the final position.
keyframe_values.fade_out: Use opacity keyframes to fade captions out before dense animation rather than cutting them off harshly.
keyframe_values.tracking: Avoid aggressive tracking changes on small one-word captions; test any tightened style at phone size.

sound.rule: Caption timing follows audible speech; music and SFX must not make captions carry normal intelligibility.

captions.rule: Use clean sans styling, consistent size, and phone-safe placement; remove duplicate captions when another text layer carries the idea. Track styles can save brand caption styling after one caption is designed.

color.rule: Use high contrast fill, stroke, shadow, or backing so captions stay readable over bright and dark footage.

implementation.ffmpeg: Split transcript into short chunks, burn captions after overlays, and inspect phone-size contact sheets for collisions.
implementation.remotion: Store word chunks with maxChars, maxDurationFrames, lowerThirdSafeRegion, styleId, and popFade keyframes.
implementation.blender: Use text objects for selected animated caption moments only; keep accessibility subtitles separate when needed.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Generate auto captions, shorten chunks manually, apply a clean style, then use a subtle pop/fade animation only where readable.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Window > Text > Captions and Create Captions from Transcript, set short single-line captions, correct transcript and punctuation, style one caption, create a track style, upgrade to graphics if needed, then disable or opacity-fade captions over dense animation sections.

common_mistakes: Converting captions to graphics before correcting transcript errors.
Using one-word chunks where longer subtitle lines would be clearer.
Letting pop animation finish after the spoken word has already passed.
Placing lower-third captions over hands, faces, products, or proof.
Applying a caption preset to every layer without checking collisions.
Leaving captions active over a full-screen animation that already says the same words.
Using the same pop emphasis on filler words and impact words.
qc: Caption wording and timing were corrected before graphic conversion.
One-word chunks are readable at phone size.
Pop-fade motion finishes before the word needs to be read.
Captions do not cover faces, hands, products, proof, or platform UI.
Duplicate caption text is removed when hook text or B-roll text already carries the idea.
Caption graphics are disabled or faded over dense animation sections.
Any word-level styling lands on the word that changes meaning.
